[{"id":"nnvMTG5Sl5","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"🌐Website Manual","col":12}},{"id":"B-CtTCmVDX","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"The website module consists of two main features: a public website, and a user portal.","col":12}},{"id":"fAFxFk8rny","type":"header","data":{"text":"🌎Website","col":12}},{"id":"WCW6FzkHwB","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"The public facing website is accessible by anyone and can be dynamically updated based on information in the Church App (i.e. Beliefs, Missionaries, Ministries, etc).
The top of the Web Site workspace shows the home page as a visitor sees it. Click the preview to open the website in a new tab.
User accounts with \"Church Manager\" permissions can modify the website by editing the website settings and publishing documents.
The website menu is the Top Bar Items table in Website Settings, and pages themselves are Web Page records. Publishing a Web Page adds it to the end of the menu. Un-publishing or deleting one removes its links from the menu and footer. A message confirms each change. Rename or move the new item in the Top Bar Items table. Editing a page that is already published does not put it back on the menu. Removing a link from the menu does not take its page down: after you save, the app offers to un-publish any Web Page that link pointed at. Answer No to keep the page reachable by its address.
The shipped pages (Home, Beliefs, Sermons, Missions, Ministries) are yours to edit; an upgrade leaves your wording alone and only ever repairs the record-reading code inside a page. Open one under Web Page: the content is in Main Section (HTML), a Jinja template (Content Type HTML with Dynamic Template on) that reads your published records, so the page updates itself as you publish sermons, beliefs, missionaries and so on. Prefer to write a page by hand? Switch Content Type to Rich Text or Markdown. Per-page styles go in the Custom CSS tab; the site-wide look is the Website Theme. To restore a shipped page's original look, copy its template from the app source (churchit/patches/after_install/templates/) back into Main Section (HTML).
No user account is required to view the website - anyone with an internet connection and a web browser can view the public website.
The site's look is a Website Theme, chosen under Website Settings → Website Theme: Churchit (the shipped look) or Frappe's plain Standard. Each has a light and a dark mode; visitors switch with the sun/moon button in the navbar, and the site follows their device setting until they do.
Every page ends with the same short footer: the church's name and founding year from the Church record on the left; the phone number from Contact Us Settings and the church address on the right (the address opens in OpenStreetMap); the copyright from Website Settings → Footer, if set, in the middle; and the footer links from the same tab centred underneath. The Contact Us page shows that same church address unless Contact address differs from the church address is checked in Contact Us Settings, which reveals fields for a different one.
Any field shown outside the desk is marked beside its label: an outgoing-link badge when anyone can see it, a people badge when only signed-in members can. Hover the badge to see which pages or portal forms show that field, and click it to open one. The marks are read from the pages themselves, so a page, portal form or public link added later is marked without anyone listing it.","col":12}},{"id":"r11MenuHead","type":"header","data":{"text":"🧭 Add an Item to the Website Menu","col":12}},{"id":"r11MenuText","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Some pages are not in the website menu by default, for example the Announcements page (/announcements) and the Watch Live page (/live). A Church Manager, or any user with the Website Manager role, can add them:
1. Open Website Settings and click the Navbar tab.
2. In the Top Bar Items table, click Add Row.
3. In Label, type the name to show in the menu, for example Announcements or Watch Live.
4. In URL, type the address of the page, for example /announcements or /live.
5. Click the edit icon at the end of the new row and tick Align Right. The menu items that Churchit installs have this box ticked, so the new item then shows next to them. When you publish a page, Churchit adds its item without this box ticked, and that item shows on the left. Tick Align Right on that item too to show it with the others.
6. To move the item, drag its row up or down.
7. Save.
When a page is off in Church Features, the menu does not show its item. With more than one church, the item opens the page of the church that the visitor selected.","col":12}},{"id":"calFeedHeader1","type":"header","data":{"text":"📅 Calendar Feed","col":12,"level":4}},{"id":"calFeedText01","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"The Calendar page has two buttons above the calendar. Subscribe adds the calendar to the calendar app of a phone or computer. Download .ics saves the calendar as a file. Both give the calendar of the church that the page shows, without its branch churches. The link is https://<your site>/api/method/churchit.ics.get_public_calendar.
- The feed shows the same functions as the Calendar page: published functions from one month ago to six months ahead, with their address, description and online meeting link. Functions with Link Only ticked are not in the feed.
- With more than one church, add ?church=<church ID> to show the calendar of one published church.
- Add ministry=<ministry> to show only the functions of one published ministry, for example ?church=CHR-01&ministry=Youth. A ministry that is not published gives an empty calendar.
Calendar apps check the link for changes by themselves.","col":12}},{"id":"locWebHeader1","type":"header","data":{"text":"📍 Locations (Multi-Church)","col":12,"level":4}},{"id":"locWebIntro01","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Switch on Enable Multi-Church in Church Features and the website can show all of your churches, not just the main one. Open each Church and tick Publish to put it on the website. That is the only step. A church you leave unpublished does not appear anywhere on the site.","col":12}},{"id":"locWebSwitch1","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Once two or more churches are published, a Locations item appears in the website menu. It lists every published church, and All locations at the bottom opens the Locations page, which shows a card for each church with its photo, mission statement, description and address. The photo is the Image of the Church. Visitors see it only when it is a public file. The Study manual tells how to make it public.","col":12}},{"id":"locWebFollow1","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"When a visitor picks a location, the whole website switches to that church and stays there as they move from page to page. These follow the choice:
- the church name in the website menu, and the address and phone number in the footer
- the home page, calendar, sermons, ministries, missions and bulletins
- the funds offered on the Give page
- the About Us page, which shows that church's own About and Mission Statement when it has them, and the main church's wording when it does not
- anything a visitor sends in from those pages, such as a prayer request, which belongs to the church whose page they used","col":12}},{"id":"locWebNotes01","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"A few things worth knowing:
- A record ticked Shared with all churches, such as a sermon, a song or a room, appears on every church's pages. The Foundations manual explains sharing.
- A member who is signed in sees their own church first, whether or not it is published.
- If only one church is published, or multi-church is switched off, there is no Locations item and the website looks exactly as it does for a single church.","col":12}},{"id":"r10LiveHead","type":"header","data":{"text":"📺 Watch Live","col":12}},{"id":"r10LiveText","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"To show your live stream on the website, open the Church and put the link to the stream in Live Stream Link. The link must start with https://. The /live page then shows the stream:
1. A YouTube video link, a youtube.com/channel/ link that ends in /live, a Let's Church media link, a PeerTube video link or an Owncast player link (it ends in /embed/video) plays on the page.
2. Any other link, such as a youtube.com/@name/live link, opens the site of the stream.
3. A branch church without its own link uses the link of its parent church.
4. If no church above the selected one has a link, /live shows \"Page not found\".
The Calendar page shows a Watch live button on each function with Streamed ticked while it runs. The Ministries manual tells more. The website menu has no Watch Live item by itself. To add one, see Add an Item to the Website Menu above, and use the URL /live.","col":12}},{"id":"r11LiveYouTube","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"A YouTube channel. A youtube.com/@name/live link does not play on the page. It opens YouTube. To play the stream of your channel on the page, use the link with your channel ID: https://www.youtube.com/channel/channel ID/live. A channel ID starts with UC, for example UCabcdefghijklmnopqrstuv. To find it, sign in to YouTube with the channel account and open https://www.youtube.com/account_advanced. Copy the Channel ID. You can also open your channel page, click more about this channel, click Share channel and click Copy channel ID. This link always plays the stream that is live now, so you do not change it for each service.
A channel link does not play in every browser. After you set the link, open /live and make sure that the stream plays. If it does not play, use the watch link of the stream, for example https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=video ID. A watch link plays one stream only, so put the new link on the Church before each service.","col":12}},{"id":"r10MembersHead","type":"header","data":{"text":"🔒 Members-only Pages","col":12}},{"id":"r10MembersText","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"To show a web page only to members, open the Web Page, tick Members Only and save. A visitor who is not signed in goes to the login page and comes back to the page after login. A signed-in user who is not an active member, for example a visitor or a contact, sees a Not Permitted message. Staff who can edit web pages can always open the page. A members-only page does not show in the website search.
A link to a members-only page in the menu, the footer or the portal shows only to the people who can open the page. Other visitors do not see the link or the page title, and the page is not in the site map. This applies to links that use the page route as you see it on the page form. If you type the route in a different way, for example with an accent, the link shows to everyone, but the page stays closed.","col":12}},{"id":"r10PagesHead","type":"header","data":{"text":"🔌 Turn a Website Page Off","col":12}},{"id":"r10PagesText1","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Open Church Features and open the Website Pages section. Each page that Churchit puts on the website has one row. Clear Enabled on a row and save to take that page off the website. Visitors then get \"Page not found\", the form on that page takes no new entries, and the links to the page go from the menu, the footer, the member portal and the site map. Nothing is deleted, and the records in the desk do not change. Tick Enabled again to bring the page and its links back.","col":12}},{"id":"r10PagesText2","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"When you clear a module in Church Features, its website pages go too. For example, with Study off, the Sermons, sermon, podcast, Bible and Bible Memory pages are off. Web Site is different: it hides only the desk tools, and the public website stays on. A page that you made yourself is not in this list. To take one of your own Web Pages off the website, clear its Published box. With the Sermons page off, the home page does not show the latest sermon, the link to all sermons or the sermon count. If you changed your home page, check it for links to pages that are off.","col":12}},{"id":"r10BuilderHead","type":"header","data":{"text":"🧱 Pages made with Frappe Builder","col":12}},{"id":"r10BuilderText","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Frappe Builder is a separate app to design web pages by drag and drop. A System Manager can install it next to Churchit and make new pages with it. Note the following:
1. A Builder page takes its address before Churchit pages, web forms and Web Pages. Before you use an address, open it in a private window. Use it only when it shows \"Page not found\".
2. Do not use an address that is listed under Website Pages in Church Features, also when that page is off. A page that is off shows \"Page not found\" in place of a Builder page at that address.
3. A Builder page cannot keep the records of one church apart from the others. Show church records, such as events, sermons or people, only on Churchit pages, and link to those pages from your Builder page.
4. Churchit does not put its website badge on the fields that a Builder page shows.
5. The shipped pages (Home, Beliefs, Missions, Ministries and Sermons) stay Web Pages. Churchit ships no Builder pages.","col":12}},{"id":"nZdduTPzRH","type":"header","data":{"text":"👤User Portal","col":12}},{"id":"8qBfIl0adi","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"The user portal requires login credentials and provides users a personalized interface for accessing church information relevant to their account (i.e. Personal Profile, Prayer Requests, Alms Requests, Function Sign-Ups, etc).
Portal users cannot access all information in the Church App, they can only access information related to their 'Person', or information shared with them (i.e. non-private prayer requests).","col":12}},{"id":"pSbMnu7rQe","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Each portal page shows a menu of the other portal pages. On a computer, the menu is a column on the left. On a phone, it is a row below the top bar that you scroll sideways.
The menu is the Menu table in Portal Settings. The Role on each row controls who sees it. To add, remove or move a page in the menu, change that table.","col":12}}]
